etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English enemyte, from Old French enemisté, ennemistié, from Late Latin, Vulgar Latin *inimīcitās, *inimīcitātem, from Latin inimīcus (“enemy”). Cognate with French inimitié, Portuguese inimizade, Spanish enemistad. By surface analysis, en(e)m(y) +‎ -ity.
senses: The quality of being an enemy; a hostile or unfriendly disposition.
A state or feeling of opposition, hostility, hatred or animosity.
